label: conj:partition-sum-proton-residual
title: Proton tower residual compared with $m_e\sum_{\lambda\vdash3}1/\dim_q\lambda = m_e(2 + 1/[2]_q)$
html:
Let \mathfrak{m}^{\mathrm{tower}}(\mathfrak{p}, q_0) be the pure-tower proton mass. The proton tower residual equals the electron mass times the inverse-quantum-dimension sum over partitions of 3:

    \Delta m_{\mathfrak{p}}
    \;:=\;
    m_{\mathfrak{p}}^{\mathrm{CODATA}} - \mathfrak{m}^{\mathrm{tower}}(\mathfrak{p}, q_0)
    \;\overset{?}{=}\;
    m_e\sum_{\lambda\vdash3}\frac{1}{\dim_q\lambda}
    \;=\;
    m_e\Bigl(2 + \frac{1}{[2]_q}\Bigr).

The second equality is proved, as a formal sum, in Frobenius Casimir of H_3(q) (item 4). The same proposition shows that this sum is not the Markov trace of the Frobenius Casimir of H_3(q): at z = q^3/(q^2+1) that trace is (q^4+q^2+1)(q^6+q^4+q^2+5)/(q^2+1)^2, which is 6 at q=1 where the sum is 5/2. The element C_{\dim_q} whose trace is the sum is built to have that trace, and at z = q^3/(q^2+1) it is undefined because the (1^3) block has Markov weight 0; the sum over the surviving blocks is 1+1/[2]_q. Consequently, the Markov trace of the Frobenius Casimir on H_3(q) does not equal the inverse-quantum-dimension sum over partitions.

Comparison (empirical; not part of any proved statement). At q_0, m_e(2+1/[2]_{q_0})=1.2761 MeV, and the classical value (5/2)\,m_e=1.2775 MeV.

The tower that production uses is fixed by the proton identity

  \frac{m_{\mathfrak p}}{m_e} \;=\; 2\,\frac{\mathrm{Vol}(4_1)}{\hbar_q^2}\,F_{\mathrm{Bor}}(q) \;-\; 12,
  \qquad
  F_{\mathrm{Bor}}(q) = \frac{|\mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}})|\,[3]_q!}{q^3},

whose Borromean weight y_{(2,1)} = 1/[2]_q^2 uses the canonical Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1). Its tower term is \mathfrak{m}^{\mathrm{tower}} = 2\,m_e\,(\mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\hbar_q^2)\,F_{\mathrm{Bor}}, and the residual against it is:

pin q_0 from \mathfrak{m}^{\mathrm{tower}} (MeV) \Delta m_{\mathfrak p}/m_e m_{\mathfrak p} (MeV)
proton the identity above, solved with CODATA m_{\mathfrak p}/m_e 944.404 -12 (by construction) 938.272089 (round trip)
muon m_\mu/m_e = \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\hbar_q^2, CODATA 2022 944.404 -11.99955 938.271861 (-244 ppb)

At the proton-mass anchor the residual is -12\,m_e identically, because q_0 is defined by solving the identity there; it is not an empirical test. The muon-mass anchor is the only one at which m_{\mathfrak p} is tested independently. The residual is negative, and its magnitude is set by the constant 12 in the identity rather than by a partition sum. The integer 12 is fitted: it was selected because 2\,m_\mu F_{\mathrm{Bor}}(q_0) exceeds the measured m_{\mathfrak p} by about 12\,m_e, and no derivation of a -12\,m_e term is established. It is one discrete parameter chosen against the target, and the factorisations 12 = \dim V_{(2,1)}\cdot|S_3| = 2\cdot 6 and 12 = 2F_{\mathrm{Bor}}(1) are arithmetic readings of the integer rather than derivations. Because integer multiples of m_e are spaced about 545 ppm of m_{\mathfrak p} apart, the nearest integer always lies within about 272 ppm; a miss of 244 ppb at the muon-mass anchor therefore has probability \approx 10^{-3} by chance alone, before counting the choice of the formula's other factors.

Two earlier residuals were measured against towers that no live producer reproduces. These are the archived corrected tower 936.994 MeV (Table 4), giving +1.278 MeV, and the literal 938.7228 MeV, giving -0.451 MeV. Neither tower is the z = q^3/(q^2+1) Borromean tower above. The near-match of +1.278 MeV with m_e(2+1/[2]_{q_0}) exists only against the archived value, and there the classical (5/2)\,m_e is closer (0.03\%) than the q-form (0.14\%). Against the live tower, neither sum is close to the residual.
